supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: emailservice_latency-90 z=883.6 (4418.0%); emailservice_latency-50 z=318.18 (1590.9%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=9.11 (105.0%); checkoutservice_latency-50 z=7.75 (209.2%)
traces for emailservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.19->0.19ms (1.0x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 3.63->203.89ms (56.18x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: Its latency deviation is small (p90 +105%, z=9.11) next to emailservice (p90 +4418%, z=883.6), which fits a slowdown passed downstream from its call to emailservice (E1).

Emailservice's own span self-time is unchanged (0.19->0.19ms), and E1 lists no significant CPU deviation. Only caller-observed latency rose, which points to delay on the request path rather than compute starvation (E1, E2).
Not separable from an emailservice-side delay. The slowdown appears only on calls into emailservice, and its other metrics are healthy, so this is attributed to emailservice's network path (E2).

proposed_fix.description: Inspect the emailservice pod and its sidecar for an injected network delay (e.g. a tc netem qdisc or chaos experiment) and remove it. Then confirm inbound emailservice latency drops back to about 4ms p50 and checkoutservice latency recovers. Restart the emailservice pod only if the delay cannot be removed in place.
